name: Infographic Motion SFX Sync
use_when: An explainer sequence has animated words, arrows, route traces, highlights, chart bars, screenshot swaps, or cutout entrances.
The graphic feels visually polished but sonically flat.
Small SFX can clarify hierarchy without turning the documentary into a loud social edit.
An on-screen research or process timelapse needs restrained anticipation without masking narration.
avoid_when: The subject is serious and SFX would make the explanation feel cheap or glib.
Voiceover, testimony, or source audio needs full attention.
The animation already has enough rhythm from narration and music.

timeline_pattern.pattern: lock_graphic_motion -> mark_major_entrances -> add_whoosh_tick_shutter_highlight_cues -> set_low_levels -> restore_music_vo -> full_mix_check
timeline_pattern.hierarchy_rule: Only the important graphic entrances or evidence highlights need SFX.
timeline_pattern.sync_rule: Cues should land on the visible start, reveal, swap, or arrival frame.
timeline_pattern.mix_rule: SFX should make motion feel intentional while staying clearly below narration.

motion.rule: Place cues after the animation timing is locked and after any low-FPS/posterize texture is applied.

sound.rule: Use soft whooshes for entrances/routes, ticks or marker sounds for highlights, and camera/shutter-like cues for screenshot swaps when tone allows.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: Aim for cues within 1-2 frames of important reveals or swaps.
keyframe_values.starting_level: Start infographic SFX around -12 dB below voiceover and lower if the sequence feels busy.
keyframe_values.music_exit: Cut music at a natural phrase ending when possible and add a short crossfade instead of a hard stop.
keyframe_values.cue_density: Avoid SFX on every layer; prioritize title entrance, route reveal, key highlight, chart entry, and final transition.
keyframe_values.research_riser: Use one restrained riser across a research/process timelapse only when it builds to a clear discovery or claim.

captions.rule: Do not let SFX-heavy graphic moments justify buried narration; captions are support, not a mix fix.

color.rule: No direct color rule; SFX should support the visual palette and documentary tone rather than shift it toward comedy by accident.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use adelay/atrim/amix/volume/afade to place SFX at reveal frames and maintain VO/music levels.
implementation.remotion: Store sfxEvents with frame, type, gain, fade, linkedElementId, and afterFpsTextureReview fields.
implementation.blender: Use timeline markers for title, route, highlight, chart, and screenshot events before placing SFX.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place SFX on separate audio tracks, align them to visible graphic events, adjust Basic volume, and crossfade music exits. For research overlays, add one restrained riser under the speed-up and fade before the next spoken claim.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers, separate SFX tracks, clip gain, short fades, and a full-mix review after music/VO are restored.

common_mistakes: Adding a whoosh or tick to every tiny graphic layer.
Placing SFX before the animation is locked and leaving cues off by several frames.
Letting highlight/shutter sounds compete with voiceover.
Using comedic or social-media SFX over a serious documentary explanation.
Cutting music abruptly instead of finding a natural phrase ending or crossfade.
Using a trailer-style riser under ordinary research footage that has no real discovery beat.
qc: Does each SFX cue map to a visible graphic event?
Do important cues land within 1-2 frames of the reveal, swap, or arrival?
Do SFX stay below narration and story-critical audio?
Is cue density low enough that the documentary tone remains credible?
Does music exit or crossfade cleanly around the final graphic sequence?
If a research riser is used, does it resolve into a visible discovery or claim without masking narration?
